newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Chevron opens filling station in Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Chevron opens filling station in Kazakhstan.

text.p: U.S. oil group Chevron Corp opened its first filling station outside North America in Kazakhstan's capital Almaty on Friday.

Chevron Chairman Kenneth Derr said the service station marked a further step in relations between Kazakhstan and Chevron, which since 1993 has been prospecting in Kazakhstan's huge Tengiz oilfield. Mobil Corp is also active there.
Kazakhstan President Nursaltan Nazarbayev said the filling station would be the first of many in the country.
"We agreed today that there will be many such filling stations all over Kazakhstan, at least in the near future in four cities," he said at the opening ceremony.
Ministers say the vast former Soviet republic in Central Asia, with oil reserves of 24 billion tonnes, could soon rank with countries such as Iraq or Kuwait among the world's top oil producers.
